findings.reason: the key is the section's central mechanism, and as written a node builds a key that lags the run's real next attempt and relabels a new launch as one already recorded.
findings.text: §13 keys every reservation on "the run's own last committed attempt plus one" and requires every door to "launch exactly the attempt it reserved", but `ledger.runs` returns only promoted records (`reckon/ledger.py:3128`; its sole writer is `append_run` from `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1741`), so a run whose latest attempt has ended without a promotion has no committed attempt for its key: run `r-20261108T111844665111-diiid-material-mask-limiter` sits at pointer attempt 5 with attempt-1…attempt-5 records on disk and no row under `docs/state/nova/runs/`, and the section's own reproduction fixture (attempt 1 ended, `attempt.json` naming 2) has the same shape. The key computed there is not the in-flight attempt the section is about, and because constraint 2 forbids re-deriving the launched number, a door would reserve one number and either refuse the correct attempt or relaunch an attempt number already carrying `attempt-N-worker.json`/`attempt-N-exit.json`, retiring the failed attempt's evidence under the new launch. The section needs the key stated against the record that actually names the run's next attempt (with the in-flight attempt excluded, e.g. highest ended attempt plus one, reconciled with the pointer) or must exempt never-promoted runs explicitly

response_events.note: §13 now keys on the newest attempt the run has a receipt for in its run directory, plus one, not the ledger's promoted records, so an unpromoted run like the material-mask run keys correctly; the in-flight attempt.json is excluded so racing doors share the key.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_retired_attempt_ended` (dispatch_launch.py:2072), `claim_next_attempt`/`_claim_may_be_reclaimed` (resumption.py:389/366), the `attempt = int(previous_attempt) + 1` block with `prior_node_runs` filtered by node id (dispatch.py:2707–2743), `_create_worktree` (dispatch.py:2834), `supervised_launch` (dispatch_launch.py:2640) and `record_resumption` (dispatch_sessions.py:2422) all resolve and match what the section says of them.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the section reproduces the window before repairing it, lists one measurable case per hazard, and names a logged negative control for each case, including the new older-run case and its "keying the dispatch on the node's newest committed run" control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate and control log is written under the run directory, and the armed-suite comparison is kept in the base tree, so no evidence sits in a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach the symbols, paths or test name the section introduces.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated key source, "the run's own last committed attempt plus one", is a lagging record that does not name the attempt a door is about to launch.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: a per-attempt reservation that refuses a concurrent launch of the same run and frees itself by liveness.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `f-arolw-013` names all four source paths plus the new test, and §13's upstream (§12) has landed, so the section declares no unmet edge.
